chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maymūn, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

Zakat al-fiṭrah is one sāʿ of dates, or one sāʿ of raisins, or one sāʿ of barley, or one sāʿ of dried curds, on behalf of every person, free or slave, young or old. And there is no blame upon one who does not find what he can give in charity.

key_terms.أَقِطٍ: dried curds as one valid staple for payment
key_terms.تَمْرٍ: dates as one valid staple for payment
key_terms.حَرَجٌ: blame or hardship removed from the one unable to pay
key_terms.زَبِيبٍ: raisins as one valid staple for payment
key_terms.زَكَاةُ ٱلْفِطْرَةِ: the alms due at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.شَعِيرٍ: barley as one valid staple for payment
key_terms.صَاعٌ: a prescribed measure for the payment amount

ai.seo_question: What is the required amount of zakat al-fiṭrah, and is it waived for the poor?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal amount and common food types for zakat al-fiṭrah, making it due on behalf of every individual regardless of age or social status. It also clarifies that a person who cannot find anything to give is under no hardship or blame.
